headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; Cline’s filesystem/MCP/browser tools can be steered by gpt-researcher outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads/writes workspace files and uses MCP, while gpt-researcher can emit reports and citations from research tasks. Their shared filesystem bridge makes attacker-controlled content from B plausibly reach A as trusted instructions. This is not proven by docs to be default-manual only, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher writes a report into the same workspace Cline reads
IF Cline parses file contents or MCP payloads as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Store B outputs in a separate directory Cline does not scan
Add a manual review step before Cline consumes B-generated files
Disable MCP endpoints that accept untrusted text
Prefix B outputs with a fixed non-executable template
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read local files and have broad network egress; Cline also handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while gpt-researcher sends queries and documents to external APIs. In a shared workspace, sensitive source code or documents can flow into B’s outputs and then out over B’s APIs, creating a medium leakage path.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local documents or workspace files
IF gpt-researcher uploads those documents or derived excerpts to external APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files outside the shared workspace
Restrict B to non-sensitive folders only
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing
Review B’s export settings before running it on private data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or mutate shared workspace state: Cline explicitly modifies git state and filesystem, and gpt-researcher can read files and run subprocesses in a research task. With shared filesystem state and no locking documented, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git/work products. The overlap is dangerous by default in a shared workspace.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory
IF either agent writes files or git state without external locking
mitigations: Run the agents in separate workspaces
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Check for dirty-tree changes before each write
requires-engineering: add file locks or a task orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on tool outputs, and gpt-researcher produces reports, citations, and synthesized findings that Cline may treat as authoritative. Because B’s output can become A’s input without a built-in verification boundary, mistaken or hallucinated research can cascade into code or browser actions. The pair is not documented as mutually verifying, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Cline uses gpt-researcher reports as factual ground truth
IF no human or automated verification step checks citations before action
mitigations: Require source-link review before acting on B’s report
Have Cline summarize B’s claims before execution
Limit B to draft-only outputs
Spot-check citations against original sources
requires-engineering: add automated fact-verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while gpt-researcher handles research queries, local documents, and multiple external APIs. If regulated or region-bound documents are placed in the shared workspace, B’s API calls can move them to third-party services and Cline may retain screenshots or logs. The profiles do not document matching residency or retention controls, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential documents are processed by gpt-researcher
IF Cline stores screenshots or logs containing regulated data
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared workspace
Disable screenshot capture for sensitive tasks
Confirm API-region and retention settings before use
Delete generated reports after review
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention policy
